modules.title: Module K1 — Quality index
modules.subtitle: The QEI slot in the renal toolbox — registered, always N/A, and the four reasons it ships empty.

slides.heading: The QEI slot — and why it is empty
slides.lead: This is the module where the anchor metric should live, and I want to be straight about it up front: in the kidney it is empty, and that is a substrate problem, not a missing-effort problem.
slides.why: Leaving a silent hole where a reviewer expects the anchor metric would let the Stream-B verdict be read as if a QEI stood behind it — it does not.
slides.note: QEI works in brain because it stands on continuous GM/WM/CSF probability maps and a spatial prior spCBF = 2.5·GM + 1.0·WM. The kidney supplies two binary, hand-drawn masks and no probability map at all, so the structural term of QEI has nothing to correlate against.
slides.provenance: Nery et al. 2020 (MAGMA, PARENCHIMA) — 59 consensus statements, ZERO numeric image-quality thresholds; exhaustive term scan finds no `quality control`, `CoV`, `cut-off`, `DVARS` or `framewise`, and `tSNR` only qualitatively.

slides.heading: K1.1 — Renal composite quality index · REGISTERED, ALWAYS N/A IN v1
slides.lead: This check asks whether there is a single 0-to-1 number summarising renal perfusion-map quality the way QEI does for brain — and in version one it answers no, out loud, in the report.
slides.why: It stops the absence of a renal anchor metric from being an unexplained gap, so no reader mistakes a Stream-B verdict for one that had a quality index behind it.
method: Accept whatever was supplied — RBF map, cortex masks, medulla masks — and consume none of it; the answer does not depend on the inputs.
Return N/A unconditionally, with the four blockers attached. No arithmetic runs at all.
Emit the ids of the checks that carry the individually-computable pieces, so the reader is routed to what does exist instead of seeing an unexplained gap.

Do NOT form a composite from those pieces — that is a decision, not a deferral: a geometric mean of three uncalibrated components is less interpretable than its components, and none of the three has a validated scale to be averaged on.

modules.title: Module K2 — Noise & distribution
modules.subtitle: Three checks on the renal perfusion map: how stable the subtraction is, how big it is relative to M0, and how much of it is physically impossible.

slides.heading: Module K2 — Noise & distribution
slides.lead: K2.1 asks how stable the subtraction is across repetitions, K2.2 asks whether the difference signal is a sensible fraction of the calibration image, and K2.3 asks what fraction of the map is physically impossible.
slides.why: All three are Stream B — they read the perfusion map, not the acquisition. Stream A is richly evidenced by the renal consensus; Stream B is not. Nery et al. 2020 (MAGMA, PARENCHIMA) carries 59 consensus statements and zero numeric image-quality thresholds, so every band in this module ships UNCALIBRATED and each slide says so rather than manufacturing a bound to look symmetrical with the brain doc. Two published statements do constrain the shape of the output: R10.1 (0% abstentions, 100% agreement) requires cortical values reported separately for left and right kidney, so every metric here is {left, right} and never a pooled scalar; R10.2 (14% abstentions, 89% agreement) declares medullary RBF unreliable, so cortex is the graded ROI and medulla is INFO only.
method: K2.1 temporal SNR — report-only, emits INFO, never a verdict
K2.2 perfusion-weighted signal as % of M0 — PASS / WARN, never FAIL
K2.3 implausible-value and negative-voxel fraction — the only Stream-B check that can FAIL on perfusion values
slides.provenance: R10.1 (0% abstentions, 100% agreement, p.8) — per-kidney reporting. R10.2 (14% abstentions, 89% agreement, p.8) — cortex is the anchor ROI.

slides.heading: K2.1 Temporal SNR (tSNR) — REQUIRED, report-only
slides.lead: How stable is the perfusion-weighted signal across repetitions?
method: Drop non-finite volumes and record n_pairs_used per kidney — it can differ per side if K7.2 already rejected pairs on one side only.
Voxelwise mu = numpy.mean(dM, axis=3) and sd = numpy.std(dM, axis=3, ddof=1) over the repetition axis.
tsnr_voxel = mu / sd, excluding sd <= 0 voxels, then average over the ROI — cortex when a cortex mask exists, whole kidney otherwise.
Emit definition and per_repetition: True inside the metric, with the full acquisition context, because renal tSNR is not comparable across papers otherwise.
Report per kidney. Never pool, never compare left against right. Then emit INFO and stop — no band is applied.

  "delta_m_4d":   "NIfTI 4D float",   # (X, Y, Z, n_pairs) per-repetition C-L subtractions
  "kidney_masks": {"left": "NIfTI 3D bool", "right": "NIfTI 3D bool"},
  "cortex_masks": {"left": "NIfTI 3D bool", "right": "NIfTI 3D bool"},  # optional, preferred
  "context": {"labelling": "FAIR", "field_T": 3.0,

}

verdicts.when: always, when it runs — the numbers and their context are reported, never graded
no 4D series (a single averaged map has no temporal axis), no mask, or fewer than 3 usable repetitions

slides.note: No band is set, for two specific reasons. (1) The definitions are not the same quantity: Buchanan's tSNR divides by the SD across the 25 ASL pairs — per-repetition — while an averaged map built from 25 pairs has roughly sqrt(25) = 5x higher SNR, so a copied threshold would be about 5x too strict and would fail nearly every good kidney scan. (2) Published values span about 7x (0.17 to 3.54), driven by ROI, field strength, labelling, readout and repetition count — not by data quality. It never falls back to a whole-image tSNR: outside the kidney the denominator is noise.
slides.provenance: UNCALIBRATED — no renal tSNR cutoff exists. Definition from harteveld2020 and garciaruiz2025. Reference context only: cortex 3.54 ± 0.71 at 1.5 T, 3.33 ± 0.54 at 3 T (garciaruiz2025, n=16); cortex 1.5–2.6 (buchanan2018, n=10); whole kidney 0.60 ± 0.15 rising to 0.93 ± 0.22 with heavy BS (bones2019, n=9); medulla 0.17 ± 0.14 (franklin2021). Per-kidney reporting mandated by R10.1 (0% abstentions, 100% agreement).

slides.heading: K2.2 Perfusion-weighted signal as % of M0 — REQUIRED
slides.lead: Is the ASL difference signal a physically sensible magnitude relative to the calibration image — the renal analogue of "does this look like ~1% ASL contrast?"
method: Gate on space first: if K4.2 reports ΔM and M0 are not on the same grid and no transform was supplied, return UNKNOWN — a ratio across mismatched grids is a number about interpolation, not labelling.
For each kidney and each available ROI: PWS% = 100 · mean(delta_m[roi]) / mean(m0[roi]), using numpy.nanmean on both.
If mean(m0[roi]) <= 0, return UNKNOWN for that kidney — the denominator is not a PD signal.
Grade the cortical value only against the 0.5–8% band. Medulla is INFO (R10.2); whole-kidney is INFO (R10.1 asks for cortex).
If pld_or_ti_s is absent, compute and report but demote to INFO — PWS falls by roughly 3× between PLD 0.5 s and 1.5 s in the same subjects. Take the worse of the two kidneys and name the side.
slides.input_json:
{
  "delta_m":      "NIfTI 3D float",   # the mean subtraction across pairs
  "m0":           "NIfTI 3D float",   # calibration / PD image, same grid
  "kidney_masks": {"left": "NIfTI 3D bool", "right": "NIfTI 3D bool"},
  "cortex_masks": {"left": "NIfTI 3D bool", "right": "NIfTI 3D bool"},  # optional, preferred
  "medulla_masks":{"left": "NIfTI 3D bool", "right": "NIfTI 3D bool"},  # optional, INFO only
  "pld_or_ti_s":  1.4,               # required to interpret; None -> reported, not graded
  "n_bs_pulses":  3,                 # optional; BS scales dM and M0 differently
}

verdicts.when: cortical PWS within 0.5–8% on both kidneys
cortical PWS outside 0.5–8% on either kidney — labelling weak, or M0 mis-scaled
cortical PWS ≤ 0 on either kidney — points at a subtraction-sign failure; cross-check K5.3
never — every bound here is uncalibrated, and a low PWS at a long PLD is a legitimate physiological finding, not a defect
computed but pld_or_ti_s unknown, so the band cannot be applied honestly
no M0, no mask, ΔM and M0 not co-registered, or mean(M0[roi]) ≤ 0

slides.note: Catches labelling failure, wrong subtraction sign, M0 scaling errors, and background suppression far more or less aggressive than declared. n_bs_pulses is recorded with the metric and a BS-heavy acquisition is annotated rather than re-banded — there is no published BS-conditioned PWS band to re-band onto.
slides.provenance: The 0.5–8% band is UNCALIBRATED — drawn to contain the full published spread, not fitted. References: cortex 2.95 ± 0.56% (1.5 T) and 3.09 ± 0.59% (3 T), medulla 1.36 ± 0.15% and 1.40 ± 0.19% (garciaruiz2025, n=16); whole kidney 3.43 ± 1.43% (radovic2022); cortex peak 5.98 ± 0.70% (bones2021); paediatric 1.5 ± 0.61% at PLD 0.5 s falling to 0.51 ± 0.27% at PLD 1.5 s (harteveld2022); review statement "typical renal cortex perfusion-weighted signal intensity of 5% of the control image signal" (odudu2018). Measured values sit below the quoted 5%. Cortex-only grading follows R10.2 (14% abstentions, 89% agreement); medulla and whole-kidney are INFO (R10.1, 100% agreement).

slides.heading: K2.3 Implausible-value and negative-voxel fraction — REQUIRED
slides.lead: What fraction of within-kidney voxels are physiologically impossible?
method: Unit guard before any arithmetic: the published clip is stated per 100 g at origin and re-cited per 100 mL elsewhere — different normalisations, ~1.05 g/mL apart. If units is not declared, return UNKNOWN; do not guess.
Select the graded ROI: cortex where a cortex mask exists, whole kidney otherwise, and record which in roi.
neg_frac = numpy.count_nonzero(rbf[roi] < 0) / rbf[roi].size
over_ceiling_frac = numpy.count_nonzero(rbf[roi] > 500) / rbf[roi].size
Score each kidney; the verdict is the worse of the two, naming the side. Do not clip the map — this is QC: it reports how much of the map is impossible, repair is the quantification pipeline's job.

verdicts.when: negative fraction < 5% and ceiling-exceedance fraction < 5%, on both kidneys
either fraction in 5–20% on either kidney
negative fraction > 20% on either kidney — a majority-negative perfusion map is not a perfusion map; cross-check K5.3 for a control/label inversion
no mask, units not declared, or fewer than 20 ROI voxels

slides.note: This is the only Stream-B FAIL that grades perfusion values at all — the other two (K4.1 empty or overlapping masks, K4.2 grid mismatch) are structural. The FAIL is licensed by the sign, not by the 20%: negative perfusion is impossible, and the 20% only sets how much noise-driven negativity is tolerated. A reader unwilling to let an uncalibrated fraction gate a FAIL can set strict=False, which demotes it to WARN. On a raw ΔM rather than a quantified map, K5.2's structure field gates it: the negative half runs, the ceiling half reports None. Catches control/label swap, subtraction sign errors, vascular contamination and gross quantification-constant errors.
slides.provenance: The 0–500 voxel window is IMPLEMENTATION — real and published (Gullaksen 2023, applied in olsen2025), but a per-voxel preprocessing clip inside one study's segmentation step, not a validated scan-level quality bound. The 5% / 20% cut-points are UNCALIBRATED: nobody publishes "reject the scan if X% of cortical voxels are negative"; they are carried from the brain module (10%/20%) and tightened to 5% because renal cortical ROIs are small. Ceiling plausibility context: whole-kidney flow ~1200 mL/min ≈ 400 mL/100 g/min in a 70 kg adult with a 300 g kidney (odudu2018). Per-kidney reporting: R10.1 (0% abstentions, 100% agreement).

modules.title: Module K3 — Perfusion level & cortico-medullary contrast
modules.subtitle: The three checks that grade the perfusion number itself — cortical level per kidney, cortex-vs-medulla separation, left-vs-right consistency. Every threshold here ships UNCALIBRATED, so no K3 check can FAIL.

slides.heading: Module K3 — Perfusion level & cortico-medullary contrast
slides.lead: This is the module where the toolbox finally looks at the perfusion number itself — and it is the module where the published evidence runs out, so all three checks report, contextualise and flag, but not one of them is allowed to fail a scan.
slides.why: K3 turns an RBF map plus masks into the one quantity the renal consensus actually asks you to report, and into two independent cross-checks on whether that quantity was measured from the right tissue.
slides.note: The obvious question: why is there no FAIL anywhere in the flagship Stream-B module? Because Nery 2020 — 59 consensus statements, the renal equivalent of the 2015 ASL White Paper — contains zero numeric image-quality thresholds. Two consensus rules do transfer, and they shape the whole module: R10.1 (100%) fixes the quantity and the per-kidney data model, R10.2 (89%) demotes anything medullary out of verdict-carrying territory.
slides.provenance: R10.1 (0% abst / 100%) and R10.2 (14% abst / 89%) set the structure; every numeric threshold in K3 is UNCALIBRATED — no published renal image-quality bound exists.

slides.heading: K3.1 · Cortical RBF level, per kidney
slides.lead: K3.1 asks the one question the renal consensus explicitly instructs us to report on: is cortical renal blood flow, for each kidney separately, a physiologically possible number?
method: Refuse to run without a declared `units` field → UNKNOWN; per 100 g and per 100 mL differ by the ~1.05 g/mL tissue density.
Per kidney, over the cortex mask: nanmean, nanstd(ddof=1) and nanmedian — the median because the consensus explicitly asks for it in skewed RBF distributions.
Also compute the whole-kidney mean and emit it clearly labelled as NOT the consensus quantity, so a user with only whole-kidney masks still gets a number.
Report left and right separately; no pooled mean is emitted at all, so nothing downstream can accidentally use one (R10.1).

Grade only against the wide 50–500 sanity band: inside → INFO with full acquisition context attached; outside → WARN. No low-side FAIL — a thin cortex partial-volumes downward, which is anatomy, not data quality.
slides.input_json:
{
  "rbf_map":      "NIfTI 3D float",
  "cortex_masks": {"left": "NIfTI 3D bool", "right": "NIfTI 3D bool"},
  "kidney_masks": {"left": "NIfTI 3D bool", "right": "NIfTI 3D bool"},   # fallback ROI, reported only
  "units":        "mL/100g/min",       # REQUIRED
  "context":      {"labelling": "FAIR", "field_T": 3.0, "pld_or_ti_s": 1.9,
                   "subject_age": 51, "native_or_transplant": "native",
                   "lambda": 0.9, "alpha": 0.95, "t1_blood_s": 1.65},
}

verdicts.when: cortical mean within 50–500 — value reported with its acquisition context, no quality claim made
cortical mean outside 50–500 mL/100 g/min on either kidney — a sanity bound, not a normal range
never — no per-scan reference interval exists
no cortex mask but a whole-kidney mask exists — the whole-kidney mean is reported and explicitly not graded
no mask at all, `units` undeclared, or fewer than 20 cortical voxels

slides.provenance: R10.1 (0% abst / 100%) mandates the quantity; the 50–500 band itself is UNCALIBRATED — 139–427 is a spread of cohort means across 53 studies (odudu2018, p.2), not a per-scan reference interval.
slides.why: Catches gross quantification errors, wrong constants, wrong units, and a mask placed outside the kidney — without ever pretending to detect abnormal perfusion.
slides.note: Why no FAIL, and no tighter band? Technical factors move this number more than disease does. In the same 15 subjects, same session, FAIR gave 362 ± 57 vs pCASL 201 ± 72 mL/min/100 g (P < 0.001, harteveld2020) — larger than any healthy-vs-diseased or adult-vs-child difference in this entire evidence base. Field strength moves it ~11%, age ~20%, ROI convention ~7%, quantification constants ~22%. And the PET reference standard itself disagrees with ASL by limits of agreement of ±136 mL/min/100 mL (olsen2025). There is also no cross-centre reproducibility study at all (odudu2018, p.4).

slides.heading: K3.2 · Cortico-medullary ratio (CMR) — a segmentation-integrity flag
slides.lead: K3.2 divides mean cortical RBF by mean medullary RBF per kidney — and because the consensus itself declares medullary values unreliable, that ratio is allowed to say the two masks are drawing from the same tissue, and nothing more than that.
method: If no medulla mask is supplied but a quantitative T1 map is, derive one inside the kidney mask: medulla is the high-T1 compartment, split at 1247 ms at 3 T or 1067 ms at 1.5 T; tag mask_source "derived_from_t1" and mark the verdict provisional.
Per kidney: cmr = nanmean(rbf[cortex]) / nanmean(rbf[medulla]).
Guard the denominator — if medulla_mean ≤ 0, or the medulla mask has fewer than 10 voxels, return UNKNOWN for that kidney rather than dividing.
Emit both compartment means alongside the ratio, so a reader can see which side is anomalous: a CMR of 1.2 from a low cortex is a different problem from one from a high medulla.
Interpret only in the low direction: cmr < 1.5 → WARN, "cortex and medulla masks may not be separated". High CMR is never flagged, and this check never FAILs or escalates beyond a WARN about masks.
slides.input_json:
{
  "rbf_map":       "NIfTI 3D float",
  "cortex_masks":  {"left": "NIfTI 3D bool", "right": "NIfTI 3D bool"},
  "medulla_masks": {"left": "NIfTI 3D bool", "right": "NIfTI 3D bool"},   # or derived from t1_map
  "t1_map":        "NIfTI 3D float | None",   # ms; used to derive medulla when no mask is supplied
  "field_T":       3.0,                        # selects the T1 split point
}

verdicts.when: CMR ≥ 1.5 on both kidneys — reported, no quality claim made
CMR < 1.5 on either kidney → "cortex and medulla masks may not be separated" — a statement about the masks, not about the kidney
never, on any input
no medulla mask and no T1 map — the consensus default protocol produces cortex ROIs only, so this is the common case and must not be penalised
medulla mean ≤ 0, or either mask has too few voxels to average

slides.provenance: R10.2 (14% abst / 89%) is what demotes it to a mask flag; the 1.5 trip point is UNCALIBRATED — no paper states a cortex:medulla ratio threshold for any purpose.
slides.why: Catches cortex and medulla masks that are not actually separated — the dominant renal segmentation failure, with a published worked example in Hammon's own admission that "the segmentation of the medulla may contain parts of the cortex".
slides.note: This is the brain GM/WM ratio in form — scale-free, robust to global scaling errors — but deliberately not in role. In brain, GM/WM < 1 is a published data-quality FAIL. Here R10.2 makes the denominator unreliable, so the ratio may only speak about the ROIs. Two supports: only ~10% of renal blood flow perfuses the medulla, so a CMR near 1 is anatomically impossible; and CMR is not even monotone with disease — it rises 1.57 → 2.01 in one CKD cohort and falls 2.08 → 1.75 in another. It is also the one Stream-B check a global scaling error cannot fool, which is exactly why it is worth having alongside K3.1.

slides.heading: K3.3 · Left-vs-right consistency
slides.lead: K3.3 compares the two kidneys against each other, because a one-sided failure of masks, registration or motion correction is invisible to every per-kidney check — each side looks perfectly consistent on its own.
method: Take the two cortical means from K3.1. If either is UNKNOWN, this check is UNKNOWN — it never substitutes a whole-kidney mean, which would mix an ROI effect with a physiological one.
Compute AI = (L − R) / (0.5·(L + R)), the standard normalised-difference definition, identical to the brain asymmetry check.
Compare abs(AI) against 0.20.
Report which side is higher, because the expected normal bias has a direction — left > right — so a right-higher asymmetry of the same size is marginally more interesting.

Never FAIL, and grade perfusion only: arterial transit time does differ significantly between kidneys with FAIR even when perfusion does not, so an ATT asymmetry check would fire on normal physiology.

verdicts.when: |AI| > 0.20 → flag for human review; may be one-sided mask/registration failure or real unilateral pathology
never — asymmetry is a review flag, not a rejection
n_kidneys == 1 (transplant, nephrectomy, agenesis)
either kidney's cortical RBF is unavailable

slides.provenance: UNCALIBRATED — 0.20 is set above the largest observed normal left>right bias (~9–13% across three PET/MR sessions) and comfortably above the cortical between-visit CV of 4–13% (odudu2018, p.3).
slides.why: Catches one-sided mask, registration or motion-correction failure — the failure mode invisible to every per-kidney check. Genuinely asymmetric pathology is surfaced for review rather than graded.
slides.note: Why tolerate as much as 20%? Four independent cohorts find no significant left–right perfusion difference (P = 0.93 FAIR, P = 0.52 pCASL, within-subject r = 0.83/0.94), but a consistent small left > right bias does exist — 0.5–6.8% in four Table-S1 studies, left higher in four of four, and 9–13% across three PET/MR sessions. A tolerance tighter than ~13% would fire on normal anatomy. And a genuinely large asymmetry may be renal artery stenosis or a single functioning kidney: a clinical finding, not an image defect.

modules.title: Module K4 — Masks & co-registration
modules.subtitle: Three REQUIRED structural gates: is the mask sane, is everything in one space, and how many slices survived?

slides.heading: Module K4 — Masks & co-registration
slides.lead: Every Stream-B number is a mean over a mask, in a space, across slices. K4 checks all three before any of those numbers are believed.
method: K4.1 per-kidney mask integrity — REQUIRED: one connected component per kidney, non-empty, non-overlapping, inside the FOV, thick enough for a cortical mean.
K4.2 ASL ↔ M0 and per-kidney registration — REQUIRED: same grid, and registration done per kidney, because the two kidneys move independently.
K4.3 slice coverage / usable-slice fraction — REQUIRED: how many acquired slices actually survived to contribute to the reported value.
K4.2 is the one place in Stream B carrying hard consensus backing (R8.1, 13% abst / 100% agreement). K4.1's thickness and voxel-count lines and all of K4.3's cut-points are UNCALIBRATED.
slides.provenance: R8.1 (13% abst / 100%): kidneys registered separately — this has no brain analogue at all. Everything else in K4 is either a definition or UNCALIBRATED, and is labelled as such on its slide.
slides.why: The mask problems that silently corrupt every other Stream-B number — masks applied to the wrong voxels, an M0 that cannot serve as a per-voxel denominator, and a perfusion map assembled from fewer slices than were acquired.

slides.heading: K4.1 Per-kidney mask integrity
slides.lead: Are the supplied masks structurally sane — one connected component per kidney, non-empty, non-overlapping, inside the field of view, and thick enough to support a cortical mean?
method: Connected components in pure NumPy (osipy bans scipy): iterative flood fill, 6-connectivity. Report n_components and largest_component_frac — the fraction matters more than the count, because a 3-voxel speckle is a different problem from a mask split in half.
Count n_voxels. An empty mask is a FAIL, not UNKNOWN: a mask was supplied and it does not describe a kidney.
FOV-edge test over all six faces — mask[0,:,:].any() or mask[-1,:,:].any() … A kidney clipped by the FOV means the reported mean is over a truncated organ.
Overlap tests: logical_and(cortex, medulla) per kidney and logical_and(left, right). Any non-zero is a construction error, not a borderline measurement — the compartments are defined disjoint.

Cortical thickness estimate: thickness_vox ≈ cortex_volume / cortex_surface, surface counted as cortex voxel faces adjacent to non-cortex (shifted-array comparison, three axes), converted with voxel_size_mm. Verdict = the worse kidney, named by side.

  "kidney_masks":  {"left": "NIfTI 3D bool", "right": "NIfTI 3D bool"},
  "cortex_masks":  {"left": "NIfTI 3D bool", "right": "NIfTI 3D bool"},   # optional
  "medulla_masks": {"left": "NIfTI 3D bool", "right": "NIfTI 3D bool"},   # optional
  "voxel_size_mm": [3.0, 3.0, 5.0],
  "image_shape":   [96, 96, 5],
}

verdicts.when: one dominant component per kidney (largest ≥ 95% of voxels), no overlap, not FOV-clipped, ≥ 50 cortical voxels, estimated cortical thickness ≥ 2 voxels
fragmented (largest component < 95%), FOV-clipped, fewer than 50 cortical voxels, or estimated cortical thickness < 2 voxels
an empty mask, or cortex ∩ medulla non-empty, or left ∩ right non-empty
no masks supplied

slides.provenance: Structural rules (components, overlap, edge contact, empty) are definitions — nothing to tune. The ≥ 2-voxel cortical-thickness line is UNCALIBRATED, but the mechanism is consensus-published: "the reduction in cortical thickness can be severe enough such that it approaches the typical dimensions of the ASL voxels … cortical RBF results from ASL should be interpreted with caution in cases where cortical thinning is evident", with recommended in-plane resolution 2–4 mm (R6.10, 0% abst / 93%). The ≥ 50 cortical voxels floor is UNCALIBRATED — shi2026 used one cortical ROI of 70–110 voxels, so 50 sits below normal practice.
slides.note: Needs at least whole-kidney masks per side plus voxel size. Cortex/medulla tests are skipped (not failed) when those masks are absent; no masks at all → UNKNOWN. This is also why K3.1 carries no low-side FAIL: a low cortical RBF can be an artefact of anatomy meeting voxel size.
slides.why: Catches the mask problems that silently corrupt every other Stream-B number: a mask that caught bowel or liver as a second component, a kidney cut off by the FOV, cortex and medulla ROIs drawn overlapping, and a cortex too thin for the voxel size to resolve.

slides.heading: K4.2 ASL ↔ M0 and per-kidney registration
slides.lead: Are the perfusion series, the M0 and the masks actually in the same space, and was registration done per kidney?
method: Compare grids, not just matrix sizes: shapes must match on the first three dimensions AND affine_max_diff_mm = numpy.abs(A_m0 - A_asl).max() over the 3×4 geometry block must sit under a 0.01 mm float-round-trip tolerance. Two images can share 96×96×5 on different voxel sizes.

If the grids differ and no transform is supplied → FAIL: every ROI statistic would be computed over the wrong voxels, so this is a corruption, not an absence. If a transform is supplied, PASS on geometry and record it.
Read registration.scope. scope == "global" → WARN: a single rigid transform for both kidneys cannot be right, because they move independently.

Residual check when masks and the 4D series are both present: intensity-weighted centroid of each kidney mask region in the first and last volumes, distance reported in mm. Cheap, dependency-free, and it feeds K7.1 which grades displacement properly.
Verdict is the worst of: grid test, scope test, and the residual shift exceeding one in-plane voxel.
slides.input_json:
{
  "delta_m_affine": "4x4 float", "delta_m_shape": (96, 96, 5, 25),
  "m0_affine":      "4x4 float", "m0_shape":      (96, 96, 5),
  "mask_affine":    "4x4 float", "mask_shape":    (96, 96, 5),
  "registration": {                    # provenance, as recorded upstream
     "performed": True,
     "scope":     "per_kidney",        # "per_kidney" | "global" | "per_kidney_per_slice" | None
     "n_transforms": 2,
     "type":      "rigid",
  },
  "kidney_masks": {"left": "NIfTI 3D bool", "right": "NIfTI 3D bool"},
}

verdicts.when: grids match (or transforms supplied) and registration scope is per_kidney or per_kidney_per_slice
a single global rigid transform was used for both kidneys — R8.1 says they must be registered separately
residual centroid shift > 1 in-plane voxel on either kidney
grid/affine mismatch with no transform supplied — every ROI statistic would be meaningless
no affines available, or no registration provenance and no masks to run the residual test on

slides.provenance: R8.1 (13% abstentions, 100% agreement): "retrospective image registration is highly recommended", with the body note "the kidneys should be registered separately if using rigid/affine transformations as they move independently." Corroborated by bones2019 (per-kidney translation-only Euler, Elastix), bones2022 (per-subject/per-kidney/per-slice, PCA groupwise metric) and olsen2025 (per-repetition-and-kidney rigid affine). This has no brain analogue at all. Grid/affine equality is a definition; the 1-voxel residual WARN is UNCALIBRATED — the same informal line as cox2017's visual "exclude > 1 voxel movement" rule.
slides.note: Needs affines and shapes for ΔM, M0 and the masks; registration provenance for the scope test; masks plus the 4D series for the optional residual test. When scope is absent but grids match, the check returns PASS on geometry with registration_scope: None stated in the reason — a reader is never told per-kidney registration happened when nobody said it did. Caveat: heavy background suppression can break ASL-driven registration to M0 — 54% success using the BGS ASL images versus 100% using separately-acquired fat images (bones2019, n=9), so the check carries K5.2's detected background-suppression state in its reason string rather than treating registration quality as a proxy for acquisition quality.
slides.why: Catches masks applied to the wrong voxels, an M0 that cannot be used as a per-voxel denominator, and the specifically renal failure of correcting both kidneys with one transform.

slides.heading: K4.3 Slice coverage / usable-slice fraction
slides.lead: How many acquired slices actually survived to contribute to the reported value?
method: Resolve the slice axis from the affine — the array axis whose direction cosine is most nearly parallel to the slice normal. Never assume axis 2.
For each slice index along that axis and each kidney: count mask voxels, and count mask voxels where the perfusion value is finite and non-zero.
A slice counts if it has at least min_mask_voxels_per_slice mask voxels, and is usable if at least 90% of those voxels carry finite non-zero data.
usable_fraction = n_slices_usable / n_slices_with_mask, per kidney.

Report edge slices separately: how many unusable slices are first or last in the masked stack. Edge failure is a known systematic artefact, and "2 of 2 losses were edge slices" tells a user something actionable. Return N/A for 2D single-slice readout — coverage is 1/1 by construction and grading it would be theatre.
slides.input_json:
{
  "rbf_map":      "NIfTI 3D float",     # or the mean delta_m
  "kidney_masks": {"left": "NIfTI 3D bool", "right": "NIfTI 3D bool"},
  "affine":       "4x4 float",          # to resolve which array axis is the slice axis
  "readout":      "2D multislice",      # from K5.2; "2D single-slice" makes this N/A
  "min_mask_voxels_per_slice": 20,
}

usable fraction in 0.5–0.8 on either kidney
usable fraction < 0.5 on either kidney — reported prominently, still a WARN because the cut-points are uncalibrated
never on the fraction. Fewer than one usable slice per kidney is reported as UNKNOWN, since no ROI statistic exists to grade
readout is 2D single-slice (R6.1, the consensus default)

slides.provenance: 0.8 / 0.5 cut-points are UNCALIBRATED throughout — no paper states a usable-slice fraction criterion. The loss is heavily documented even though the threshold is not: in a 5-slice FAIR protocol only 48.3% of 60 single-kidney scans retained all five slices, the full distribution being 1.7% / 8.3% / 16.7% / 25.0% / 48.3% for one to five usable slices (olsen2025) — dropped by visual assessment, not by any metric. Edge slices fail systematically: "maps with significant noise were excluded (mostly generated from slices at the very beginning or end of the imaging stack, mainly due to partial volume effect with the nearby structures) … The middle slice … was the most representative one" (radovic2022). Coverage is protocol-conditional: R6.1 (10% abst / 95%) makes 2D single-slice the default, so whole-kidney coverage must never be assumed. The 90%-finite rule and the 20-voxel floor are construction choices, exposed as config.
slides.note: Needs a perfusion map or mean ΔM, kidney masks, the affine, and the readout type from K5.2. Single-slice readout → N/A; no masks → UNKNOWN.
slides.why: Catches a perfusion map assembled from fewer slices than were acquired, and the specific pattern where the losses are all at the ends of the stack — which tells the user their slab was positioned too tightly around the kidney.

modules.subtitle: Stream A. The module that works out what the scan actually is, and therefore which of the other checks are allowed to run.

slides.heading: Module K5 — Schema, data type & control/label
slides.lead: Nothing in this module grades image quality; it reads the metadata, infers the acquisition, and decides which of the other twenty checks may run at all — and K5 is where the renal evidence base is at its strongest and at its weakest on the same three slides.
slides.why: Without it, a 20-pair minimum gets enforced on a 3D scan, a QUIPSS II requirement gets applied to PCASL, and the six metadata-consuming checks guess in silence.
slides.note: K5.1 rests on the single highest-confidence citation in the whole design — Nery 2020 Table 4, agreed 81–100%. K5.2 is pure deterministic classification. K5.3 is the only check in the module that can FAIL, and its consistency bounds are UNCALIBRATED: no published renal swap threshold exists.

slides.heading: K5.1 Metadata completeness vs Nery Table 4
slides.lead: Is enough acquisition metadata present to run the checks that depend on it — and where it is absent, which checks does that silently degrade?
method: Merge the sources in priority order: sidecar, then vendor header, then affine-derived, then K5.2's inference — and record which source each item came from.
Test the 9 gating items for presence and basic unit sanity: a PLD of 1400 is ms, a PLD of 1.4 is s; normalise both to seconds and record the assumed unit.

Map each missing item to the checks it disables via a static dependency table, and emit that as checks_degraded so the consequence sits in one place instead of UNKNOWNs scattered across K2.2, K4.3, K5.3, K6.2, K6.3 and K7.2.
Count the full Table-4 set for the report, but do not grade on it.
Never FAIL, and emit organ/laterality under a clearly-named non-standard extension namespace so nothing is presented as BIDS-compliant that is not.

verdicts.when: all 9 gating items resolvable from sidecar, header or affine
one or more gating items missing — they are listed, with the checks they degrade
not reachable. No standard mandates renal ASL metadata, so its absence cannot fail a scan
no sidecar, no header and no affine — nothing to inspect at all

slides.provenance: Nery 2020 Table 4, "Minimum set of parameters to be reported in ASL studies", agreed 81–100% — PUBLISHED, and a presence test, so it needs no calibration
slides.why: It closes the upstream gap that would otherwise make the six metadata-consuming checks guess in silence.
slides.note: BIDS does not cover the kidney — kidney, renal and abdom occur zero times in BIDS v1.11.1 against 64 occurrences of brain, and there is no registered BEP for body imaging. Two traps are encoded in the reader: BIDS SliceThickness is the microscopy field in micrometres, so Nery's slice thickness maps to AcquisitionVoxelSize; and LabelingSlabThickness says "for non-selective FAIR a zero is entered" while the schema sets exclusiveMinimum: 0 — FAIR is the dominant renal PASL variant, so renal data hits this. The reader tolerates 0 and the finding is filed upstream.

slides.heading: K5.2 Data-type & geometry detection  ·  routing, emits INFO
slides.lead: What kind of renal acquisition is this, so that the right checks run and the wrong ones are marked N/A rather than failed?
method: Give every file a role from its name, rules applied in order, first match wins: mask, then m0, then calib as a prefix only, then t1map, then asl, then struct.

Classify the labelling scheme from tokens only, never by default — R3.1 endorses both PCASL and FAIR, so with no token and no sidecar the value stays "unknown" and every downstream consumer says so rather than assuming a scheme; labelling is also the comparability context K2.1 and K3.1 report against.
Read the shapes: a 3-D ASL file is a pre-subtracted deltaM; a 4-D file is a control/label series with n_pairs_implied = N // 2; any m0-role file makes M0 "separate".

Resolve orientation from the affine, not the array order: the dominant RAS component of the slice normal names the base plane, arccos of that component gives the obliquity, and 10 degrees or more adds the -oblique suffix.
Background suppression is tri-state and never confidently false; emit INFO and let each downstream check read the axes and decide its own N/A.

slides.heading: K5.3 Control vs label ordering
slides.lead: Is the control/label polarity the right way round — is the control volume brighter than the label volume, consistently, across pairs?
method: Gate first: background suppression ON → N/A, pre-subtracted ΔM → N/A, fewer than two volumes → N/A.
Split by index parity — even assumed control, odd assumed label — and write that assumption into the metric so no reader mistakes it for a measured fact; a supplied aslcontext overrides it.
Compute per pair, not pooled: c_p and l_p are nanmeans over the kidney mask, and d_p = 100·(c_p − l_p) / (0.5·(c_p + l_p)).
Grade control_brighter_fraction = count(d_p > 0) / n_pairs, and report the median d_p as the motion-robust central estimate.
Pool both kidneys for this one test only — polarity is a property of the sequence, not of an organ, and pooling doubles the voxel count behind each pair mean.
slides.input_json:
{
  "asl_4d":        "NIfTI 4D float",     # even index ASSUMED control, odd ASSUMED label
  "kidney_masks":  {"left": "NIfTI 3D bool", "right": "NIfTI 3D bool"},
  "background_suppression": False,        # True | False | None; True makes the check N/A
  "structure":     "control/label series (50 volumes)",   # from K5.2
  "aslcontext":    None,                  # honoured if supplied; nothing in v1 produces one
}

verdicts.when: control brighter in ≥ 75% of pairs
control brighter in 25–75% of pairs — inconsistent sign, motion is dominating the label difference; the subtraction may still be correct but this scan cannot confirm it
control brighter in ≤ 25% of pairs — the label slab is consistently the brighter one, so the subtraction runs backwards and every RBF value flips sign
background suppression ON, pre-subtracted ΔM, or fewer than two volumes
no 4D series, no kidney mask, or every pair mean is non-finite

slides.provenance: Control brighter than label is physics, not a tuned number, and that is what the FAIL rests on; the 75% / 25% consistency bounds are UNCALIBRATED — no published renal swap threshold exists. R7.2 (5% abst / 80%) recommends background suppression for the pairs, so this check is frequently N/A on conformant renal data.
slides.why: It catches an inverted control/label polarity — the catastrophic case where every RBF value flips negative, the same failure K2.3's >20%-negative FAIL sees from the other side.
slides.note: Stated limitation: it does NOT catch a broken alternation such as c,c,l,l — that averages to the same fraction and is invisible to an intensity comparison; only a real aslcontext catches it. The reason the brain's pooled two-slab comparison was replaced by per-pair sign counting: renal acquisitions are free breathing by consensus (R7.4, 0% abst / 76%), and volume-to-volume swings from the kidney moving through the slice can exceed a 3% label difference. The uncalibrated bounds can only make the FAIL harder to reach than the brain equivalent, never easier — an uncalibrated number that can only suppress a FAIL is a safe one.

slides.heading: Module K6 — M0 calibration
slides.lead: Everything in this module protects one number: the calibration denominator that every single voxel of the perfusion map is divided by.
slides.why: An M0 error scales the whole map by one unknown constant — and a uniformly mis-scaled map looks perfectly healthy to every ratio and fraction in Modules K2 and K3, so Stream B can never catch it.
slides.note: This is the module that transfers best from brain, and the reason is worth stating: the renal consensus imposes the SAME M0 rules as the ASL White Paper, not contrasting ones. An earlier reading suggested renal BS rules were opposite polarity to brain — that is wrong, and acting on it would have inverted a working check.
slides.provenance: R9.1 (0% abstentions, 94% agreement) M0 mandatory · nery2020 p.13 verbatim for no-labelling / no-BGS / matched readout · the 5 s rule and its correction formula are PUBLISHED, but the T1,tissue it needs is UNCALIBRATED — the consensus gives no kidney T1 anywhere.

slides.heading: K6.1 — M0 present
slides.lead: Before we grade a single RBF number, we ask whether a calibration image exists at all — the image the consensus calls mandatory.
method: Read m0_type from K5.2's detection: a file whose name contains m0 / _pd, or starts with calib. No voxel data is touched.
separate or included → PASS.
absent AND a quantified RBF map is being graded → FAIL: there is no denominator, so the numbers rest on a calibration nobody recorded.
absent AND only ΔM was supplied → WARN: no quantification is claimed, so it limits what can be checked rather than invalidating a result.
None — no detection ran — → UNKNOWN.

verdicts.when: m0_type is separate or included
m0_type is absent AND a quantified RBF map is being graded
m0_type is absent and only a ΔM / perfusion-weighted image was supplied
m0_type was never determined

slides.provenance: R9.1 — 0% abstentions, 94% agreement: "M0 acquisition is mandatory". Stronger than the brain White Paper (which only recommends a separate PD image) and stronger than BIDS (which permits M0Type: "Absent"). Presence test is binary file detection — nothing to tune.
slides.why: It stops a dataset whose RBF values were produced with no recorded calibration reference — an error that scales every voxel by an unknown constant and that no Stream-B check can see.
slides.note: Why is a FAIL allowed here when almost nothing else in this design FAILs? Agreement is ≥ 90% and the deviation invalidates rather than degrades: without a calibration image, the quantity being graded is not the quantity the protocol defines. This is one of the very few places a renal check is legitimately stricter than its brain counterpart, and it has a published warrant.

slides.heading: K6.2 — M0 acquired without labelling and without background suppression
slides.lead: Then we ask whether that calibration image was acquired clean — because background suppression destroys exactly the signal the M0 is there to provide.
method: Read BackgroundSuppression and the labelling flag from the M0 scan's OWN metadata, never from the ASL pairs' metadata — the two volumes follow opposite rules.
Both false → PASS.
Either true → FAIL: the denominator is no longer proton-density weighted, so every RBF value is scaled wrong.
Compare m0_readout against asl_readout as a string/tuple match; a mismatch is a WARN, not a FAIL.
Either flag absent → UNKNOWN. No voxel data is touched by this check.

verdicts.when: no labelling AND no background suppression on the M0, readout matched
flags clean but the M0 readout differs from the ASL readout
background suppression was ON, or labelling was applied, during the M0 acquisition
the M0's own BS / labelling flags are not recorded

slides.provenance: nery2020 p.13, verbatim: "The PD image should be acquired without labelling or BGS and using a similar readout and acquisition parameters, with the exception that a long TR should be used." Identical rule to the brain White Paper — it ports unchanged. R7.2 (5% abstentions, 80% agreement) recommends BGS for the ASL pairs, which is not a contradiction. Both flags are binary reads — nothing to tune.
slides.why: It catches an M0 mistakenly acquired with the ASL protocol's background suppression left on — a setup that quietly inflates every RBF value by a factor nobody can recover after the fact.
slides.note: Why not reuse K5.2's background-suppression inference here? Because K5.2 infers BS from the ASL folder's text, and the M0 follows the opposite rule — borrowing that flag would assert exactly the wrong conclusion. Missing M0 flags stay UNKNOWN rather than being filled in.

slides.heading: K6.3 — M0 TR ≥ 5 s, or corrected
slides.lead: And finally, whether the M0 waited long enough for tissue to recover — and if it did not, how big the correction is and how uncertain that correction really is.
method: TR ≥ 5 s → PASS, correction_factor = 1.0, nothing further to do.
TR < 5 s → compute f(T1) = 1 / (1 − exp(−TR / T1)) in pure NumPy, twice: once with the cortex T1, once with the medulla T1 for that field strength.
Defaults are the midpoints of the published wolf2018 ranges: 3 T cortex 1265 ms, medulla 1537 ms; 1.5 T cortex 953 ms, medulla 1241 ms.
Report both factors and their spread and emit WARN — do not silently apply one; applied stays False.
If a quantitative t1_map is supplied, correct per compartment using ROI-mean T1, set applied: True. Missing TR → UNKNOWN.
slides.input_json:
{
  "m0_tr_s":   3.0,          # seconds
  "field_T":   3.0,          # selects the default compartment T1s
  "t1_map":    None,         # NIfTI 3D float in ms; if present, correction is per-compartment
  "cortex_masks":  {...},    # only used when t1_map is supplied
  "medulla_masks": {...},
}

verdicts.when: M0 TR ≥ 5 s
TR < 5 s — both correction factors and their spread are reported; the correction is not applied unless a T1 map was supplied
never — the consensus states this as a correctable condition, not a disqualifying one
no M0 TR recorded

slides.provenance: The 5 s rule and the exact formula are PUBLISHED and directly portable — nery2020 p.13 verbatim: "If this image is acquired without waiting for a sufficiently (> 5 s) long recovery time (TR), the SI_PD should be corrected for incomplete relaxation ... where T1,tissue is an estimate of the kidney T1." But the consensus gives no numeric kidney T1 anywhere, so the T1 defaults are UNCALIBRATED as a choice (ranges from wolf2018).
slides.why: It catches a too-fast M0 acquisition, which gives an artificially low calibration denominator and therefore inflated RBF — flagged and quantified rather than silently corrected.
slides.note: Why report two factors instead of picking one? Kidney has two tissue T1s ~400 ms apart, so the two corrections differ by 2.6–9.6% depending on TR — comparable to the technical effects K3.1 already documents. Hiding that inside a single silent correction would inject an error the same size as the ones this design spends pages warning about. A supplied T1 map is the only path where one measured number is used.

modules.title: Module K7 — Respiratory motion & outlier rejection
modules.subtitle: The module with no brain equivalent: measure how far each kidney moved, then count what that motion actually cost.

slides.heading: K7 · Respiratory motion & outlier rejection
slides.lead: This is the module with no brain equivalent, and it is where this toolbox has the clearest opening: the consensus is unanimous that respiratory motion is the renal problem, and it specifies no method and no threshold for either half of the fix.
slides.why: Breathing moves the kidney by several voxels between frames, and an uncorrected excursion silently corrupts the very control-label pairs the averaged map is built from.
slides.note: An honest quantification of "order of magnitude", because the consensus rhetoric overstates its own numbers: measured 4D-CT excursion is 11.1 ± 4.8 mm cranio-caudal, 3.6 ± 2.1 mm AP, 1.7 ± 1.4 mm RL. Against the recommended 2-4 mm in-plane resolution that is ~3-5 voxels, not 10-20. The load-bearing part is the anisotropy, CC : AP : RL ≈ 6.5 : 2 : 1. A second cohort tracking the kidney apex reports 0.74 cm (0.45-0.98 cm) — and that parenthetical is the interquartile range, not the observed range, which is 0.10-2.15 cm. Different landmark, different number: which is why no single mm figure can anchor a renal motion threshold.

slides.heading: K7.1 · Per-kidney respiratory displacement
slides.lead: How far did each kidney move, along which axis, during the series?
slides.why: It stops a map being read as clean when the kidney it came from swam several voxels — and separates in-plane motion, which registration fixes, from through-plane motion, which it does not.
method: Resolve CC / AP / RL from the affine's direction cosines — derive the axes, never assume array-axis order.

Per kidney, per volume, take the intensity-weighted centroid inside the mask: c_t = Σ(w·x)/Σ(w) with w = max(I_t, 0). Pure NumPy, no registration needed. If per-volume transforms are supplied, use their translations instead.
Project consecutive-volume displacements c_t − c_{t−1} onto the CC, AP and RL unit vectors.
Report median and max per axis, in mm and in voxels — voxels is the decision-relevant unit, since 11 mm is catastrophic at 2 mm in-plane and tolerable at 8 mm slices.

Add through_plane_fraction, the share of displacement normal to the imaging plane. Never collapse to one scalar: an isotropic brain-FD-style sum would average away the CC axis, which carries ~6.5× the RL motion.
slides.input_json:
{
  "delta_m_4d":    "NIfTI 4D float",       # or the raw control/label series
  "kidney_masks":  {"left": "NIfTI 3D bool", "right": "NIfTI 3D bool"},
  "voxel_size_mm": [3.0, 3.0, 5.0],
  "affine":        "4x4 float",             # to resolve which axis is cranio-caudal
  "transforms":    None,                    # optional per-kidney per-volume translations
}

verdicts.when: median inter-frame CC displacement ≤ 1 voxel on both kidneys AND through-plane fraction ≤ 0.25
median inter-frame CC displacement > 1 voxel on either kidney
through-plane fraction > 0.25 on either kidney — the component registration cannot correct
not on this metric. Severity is reported here; the consequence — how many pairs it corrupted — is graded by K7.2
no 4D series, no mask, no affine, or fewer than 3 usable frames; a pre-subtracted single ΔM volume has nothing to move between frames

slides.provenance: UNCALIBRATED — there is NO published mm or voxel threshold for failing a renal ASL scan on motion; the 1-voxel line comes from cox2017's visual pipeline rule "exclude > 1 voxel movement", which never states the voxel size, and the 0.25 through-plane line is an engineering default
slides.note: Why not FD/DVARS? A measured claim: "framewise displacement" AND (kidney OR renal perfusion) AND MRI NOT brain returns 0 hits on Europe PMC. Structurally, renal motion is anisotropic, the two kidneys move independently so a single 6-DOF series is ill-defined, and brain FD converts rotations on a 50 mm head-radius sphere that is meaningless for an abdominal organ. Through-plane motion is a documented cause of total data loss: one subject of 6 excluded in franklin2021, one of 10 in bones2019.

slides.heading: K7.2 · Subtraction-outlier rate ⭐
slides.lead: How many control−label pairs were corrupted enough to reject — the direct operationalisation of R8.2, which recommends outlier rejection and specifies no way to do it.
slides.why: It measures the actual consequence of respiratory motion — how much of the acquisition was destroyed — which K7.1 cannot give, since a large excursion that registration handled costs nothing and a small one at the wrong moment costs a pair.
method: Per kidney, build the voxel-wise temporal mean and SD of ΔM across repetitions, inside the mask: mu = nanmean(dM, axis=3), sd = nanstd(dM, axis=3, ddof=1).
For each pair p, compute the fraction of within-mask voxels with abs(dM[..., p] − mu) > k · sd.
Reject the pair if that fraction exceeds the rule's limit — the default harteveld_2sd_20pct rejects when more than 20% of kidney voxels deviate beyond ±2 SD.
Run each kidney independently — one kidney can be corrupted while the other is clean — and report n_rejected, rejected_fraction, surviving_pairs and the left-right asymmetry.
Gate the surviving-pair comparison on readout: the 20-pair minimum applies to 2D only, so on a 3D readout consensus_minimum_applicable is None.
slides.input_json:
{
  "delta_m_4d":   "NIfTI 4D float",       # (X, Y, Z, n_pairs)
  "kidney_masks": {"left": "NIfTI 3D bool", "right": "NIfTI 3D bool"},
  "rule":         "harteveld_2sd_20pct",  # one of four published parameterisations
  "readout":      "2D single-slice",       # from K5.2; gates the surviving-pair comparison
  "n_pairs_acquired": 25,
}

verdicts.when: ≤ 2 pairs rejected per kidney AND (on 2D readouts) surviving pairs ≥ 20
3 or more pairs rejected on either kidney
surviving pairs < 20 on a 2D readout — the consensus minimum is no longer met after rejection
rejection count differs by more than 3 between the two kidneys — one-sided corruption
fewer than 2 pairs survive on either kidney — no averaging is possible at all
pre-subtracted ΔM, or fewer than 4 repetitions (the temporal SD is not estimable)
no 4D series or no mask

slides.provenance: R8.2 outlier rejection, 0% abst / 100% — the strongest agreement in Table 2, and it states NO criterion; the four rules are IMPLEMENTATION (harteveld2020 default, bones2021, harteveld2022 paediatric 1.5 SD, garciaruiz2025 +RMSE) and the ≤ 2-rejected PASS line is UNCALIBRATED; the 20-pair minimum is R4.7 (10% abst / 89%) and R5.12 (14% abst / 83%)
slides.note: The rule firing is not itself a defect signal — Harteveld's rule fired in 18/27 FAIR and 19/27 pCASL healthy datasets, with a maximum of 2 excluded pairs per delay. Only the count matters, and that observed ceiling in known-good data is what the PASS line is anchored on. Falling below 20 surviving pairs is a WARN and not a FAIL for two stated reasons: at 83-89% it sits below the ≥ 90% agreement bar this design requires for a FAIL, and it is an acquisition-planning number being applied to a post-hoc surviving count — a deliberate extrapolation, and this design does not escalate on its own extrapolations.

slides.heading: K7.3 · Breathing strategy & gating efficiency
slides.lead: Was a consensus-conformant breathing strategy used, and if a respiratory trace exists, how much data survived gating?
slides.why: It catches a protocol that used breath-holds against a 94%-agreement recommendation, and — where a trace exists — a gating setup accepting far fewer windows than the acquisition assumed.
method: Read breathing_strategy from metadata. It has no BIDS field, so in practice it arrives via the non-standard extension namespace defined in K5.1, or not at all.
free or triggered → PASS; paced → PASS with the strategy named in the reason, since no numbered statement endorses or discourages it; breath_hold → WARN.
If a respiratory trace and trigger times are supplied, compute 100 · n_accepted_windows / n_total_windows, accepting a window when its trigger timestamp falls inside the acceptance band of the trace.
Report that efficiency as INFO inside the metric and emit no verdict on the number at all.

verdicts.when: free breathing, or free breathing with respiratory triggering
breath-hold — R7.3 (0% abst, 94%): "Breath-hold scans are not recommended for clinical renal ASL"
never. R7.4 sits at 76%, one point above the consensus bar, and 94% for R7.3 supports a firm flag but not a rejection: breath-held renal ASL is discouraged practice, not invalid data
gating efficiency reported when a trace is present — ungraded
breathing strategy not recorded — and it has no BIDS field, so this is common

slides.provenance: R7.3 breath-hold not recommended (0% abst, 94%) drives the WARN; R7.4 free breathing preferred (0% abst, 76%); R7.5 respiratory triggering (5% abst, 95%); gating efficiency is UNCALIBRATED and never graded
slides.note: Gating efficiency is deliberately never thresholded: reference values are 50 ± 13% (coronal navigator) and 41 ± 9% (sagittal) in 10 healthy volunteers, so a "below 40-50% indicates poor compliance" rule would fail roughly half of normal scans — the cohort-mean-as-threshold error, named here so it is not re-introduced later. And a trace is never sufficient on its own: bones2020 found no one-to-one correlation between bellows signal and spurious labelling — "Some repetitions had tissue labeling without the bellows indicating motion" — so the image-derived K7.1 and K7.2 are required regardless.
